correctness.rationale: For every integer a>=1 and admissible b,c,epsilon, the explicit H is smooth on the open square, its gradient cancels along the source vector field, and its unique critical point E has a positive definite Hessian. Local Morse level curves carry genuine periodic solutions. Period coboundaries give mean x=1/2, mean r=c mean(1/A), and mean(Ar)=c. Bernoulli inequality yields a strict mean-risk/variance bound; Taylor remainder on shrinking cycles establishes coefficient optimality. General symbolic derivative identities and independent full-period numerical consistency checks are included; numerical samples are not used to prove universal quantifiers.

value.rationale: The exact symmetry N=2a+1, M=a+1 and u=1 is the natural balanced threshold in a collective-risk public-goods game; the source studies its stability boundary but not its integrable degeneracy. The integral proves a full annulus of neutral cycles, while a strict, optimally quantified increase in average failure risk despite unchanged mean cooperation supplies a policy-relevant, nontrivial structural consequence beyond generic equilibrium/Hopf or routine Jensen calculations.
